newsitem.title: THAILAND: Germans negotiate more Thai infrastructure deals.
newsitem.headline: Germans negotiate more Thai infrastructure deals.

text.p: Germany said on Monday it had begun negotiating for more contracts in the multi-billion-dollar Thai infrastructure and transport sector, where its firms are already heavily involved.
Transport Minister Matthias Wissmann told a news conference that deals were being discussed in the development of mass transportation systems for traffic-clogged Bangkok.
Thailand plans to spend US$43 billion on transport development before 2000 as part of the kingdom's eighth five-year plan.
"The talks focused on the further bilateral cooperation and the opportunities for German companies in establishing and developing an efficient infrastructure in Thailand," he said.
Germany's Siemens AG is involved in the elevated rail system under construction in Bangkok and in the road and rail-based system being developed by Hong Kong's Hopewell Holdings Plc.
The construction firm Bilfinger and Berger is also heavily involved in expressway construction in Thailand and in a proposed Bangkok subway project.
Wissmann said Germany had also concluded a maritime agreement with Thailand that would be signed next month and would provide mutual access to the ports of the two nations.

Wissmann said he had discussed with Thai officials a proposed Trans-Asian railway and three possible options for the initial phase of the project. It hopes to link Kuala Lumpur in Malaysia to Bangkok and the Laotian capital of Vientiane, and then proceed on to Hanoi in Vietnam.

The first option would see the development of a high-speed train using advanced engine and track technology to link selected cities on the route. The second option calls for a slower system by upgrading existing infrastructure and rolling stock. The third would be for a very high speed, magnetic levitation system based on existing German technology.
The rail link project was first seriously discussed at a meeting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) last December in Bangkok.

In March, ASEAN member Malaysia agreed at a Bangkok meeting of European and Asian heads of government to coordinate project development of the rail link, which would allow uninterrupted rail travel from Europe to Singapore via China and Indochina.

Wissmann said other matters discussed included the proposed development of a second international airport for Bangkok, further expressway construction, and strengthening of the Thai Airways International Ltd cooperation agreement with German carrier Lufthansa AG.
